Artificial Potential Fields

Artificial potential fields for robot motion planning. An attractive potential pulls the robot towards the goal at the origin: it grows quadratically up to the distance di (the red circle, where the two parts meet) and linearly beyond, with gain ζi. A repulsive potential pushes the robot away from each obstacle: it is 0 beyond the distance ρ0 (the white circles) and grows without bound at the obstacle, with gain ηi. The last two tabs add the attractive potential and the obstacles, as a surface and as a contour plot. Drag the coloured locators in the obstacle pad to move the obstacles; Add and Remove change how many there are. (This caption is the port's: the lecture notebook has none.)

Details

The potentials, as defined in the notebook, with the robot at (x, y), its distance D from the goal at the origin and its distance ρ from an obstacle: Uatt = ½ ζ D² for D ≤ d and d ζ (D − ½ d) beyond; Urep = ½ η (1/ρ − 1/ρ0)² for ρ ≤ ρ0 and 0 beyond. A robot following the negative gradient of the sum slides towards the goal and around the obstacles, unless it stops in a local minimum. With several obstacles their Urep add up. In the last two tabs η = 1.

Obstacles: drag a coloured locator in the obstacle pad, or press the pad to move the nearest one there; Add puts a new obstacle in a free spot and Remove takes away the selected one (ringed). A focused locator moves with the arrow keys (Shift for larger steps) and Delete removes it.

Port notes: the heights above the plot range are cut off as Mathematica does (a flat, light top on the surfaces; white in the contour plot); the curves in the last two tabs mark where the notebook's If conditions switch: red at the distance di from the goal, white at ρ0 from each obstacle. Changed from the notebook at Dr. Becker's request: a list of obstacles instead of fixed one or two, a ρ0 slider for the sum, white ρ0 circles. See the design document for how the automatic height range is chosen.

Browser port of a Mathematica notebook. All computation runs in your browser.
